title: Fingerprints and Stale Hosts
description: Produce a fingerprint report for your keypair and remove the stale 10.0.0.9 entry from known_hosts.
scenario: The staging network was renumbered and host 10.0.0.9 was retired, but your ~/.ssh/known_hosts still carries its old key — a stale entry that will one day collide with a recycled IP. Produce a fingerprint report of YOUR keypair in /home/intern/fingerprints.txt (ssh-keygen -lf), and remove the retired host from known_hosts with ssh-keygen -R.
symptoms: known_hosts contains an entry for the retired host 10.0.0.9
Nobody has a written record of the team key's fingerprint
A recycled 10.0.0.9 would trigger scary MITM warnings
mission: Write your key's fingerprint report to /home/intern/fingerprints.txt and remove the 10.0.0.9 entry from ~/.ssh/known_hosts.

hints.title: Fingerprints
hints.content: `ssh-keygen -lf keyfile` prints the bit length, SHA256 fingerprint and key type — the compact identity of a key that humans can compare.

hints.title: Retire a known host
hints.content: `ssh-keygen -R 10.0.0.9` removes every entry for that host and keeps the old file as known_hosts.old — the supported way, no manual editing.

hints.title: Report first, cleanup second
hints.content: Generate the compliance report before touching known_hosts — the report is the deliverable, the cleanup is the hygiene.

acceptance_criteria.description: the report contains the ED25519 key fingerprint
the report contains a SHA256 fingerprint string
the retired host 10.0.0.9 is gone from known_hosts
